contradicting_evidence: The latest completed hour showed BTC/ETH gains, strong taker-buy shares and a small ETH/BTC increase, allowing further rebound attempts.
Declining open interest could reduce positioning pressure rather than signal fresh bearish exposure.
Stablecoin supply remains approximately 0.61% higher over 30 days, although deployment is unconfirmed.
frozen_forecast.expected_path: A tentative downside-retest bias outweighs the evidence for durable recovery. Intermittent rebounds remain plausible, with observed altcoin participation more vulnerable than BTC; this is not a forecast that every asset declines or that sustained contraction is confirmed.
falsification_conditions: Sustained BTC/ETH recovery accompanied by stronger ETH/BTC, improving median alt returns and broadening participation would invalidate the downside tilt.
Improving settled ETF flows together with demonstrated spot-demand persistence would weaken the case that rebounds lack support.
missing_evidence: Fresh daily observations showing whether negative ETF flows and seven-day stablecoin contraction persist.
A multi-session ETH/BTC and breadth sequence distinguishing durable improvement from a brief rebound.
supporting_evidence: Current breadth is weak: 31% advanced and the median constituent return was approximately -0.45%. Positive aggregate mean returns therefore do not describe typical participation.
Large-, mid- and small-alt proxy median returns were all negative. Positive mid- and small-proxy means were heavily influenced by extreme individual gainers, not broad advances.
The latest final ETF session recorded BTC outflows of $82.4 million and ETH outflows of $69.7 million; stablecoin supply fell approximately 0.12% over one day and 0.37% over seven days.

Only 18 of 100 observed constituents outperformed BTC. Positive live-anchor funding and long/short ratios above one add positioning vulnerability, but do not independently prove an impending liquidation.
